facts.text: Concord is a residential neighborhood in mid-Staten Island, named after Concord, Massachusetts, as part of a tradition of naming Staten Island communities after New England towns.
The neighborhood grew rapidly after the opening of the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge in 1964, which connected Staten Island to Brooklyn and triggered a wave of residential development across mid-island.
Concord is close to the Staten Island Mall, New York's largest enclosed shopping center, which opened in 1973 and anchors the commercial heart of mid-island.
Like much of mid-Staten Island, Concord developed as a suburban enclave, with single-family homes lining streets that radiate outward from the island's elevated central ridge.
Staten Island's highest natural point, Todt Hill at 410 feet above sea level, is just a short distance from Concord and is the highest point on the eastern seaboard south of Maine.
